sources.title: Suicide and Lyme and associated diseases
sources.key_findings: Argues infection-driven pro-inflammatory cytokines, inflammatory-metabolic changes, and quinolinic-acid/glutamate alterations increase suicidality, and that similar pathophysiology operates in Lyme and associated diseases.
sources.relevance_notes: Primary minority source proposing an infection-specific suicide contribution; mechanism mainstream, magnitude/attribution contested.

sources.title: Suicidal and homicidal tendencies after Lyme disease: an ignored problem
sources.key_findings: Extends the neuropsychiatric-Lyme thesis to suicidal and aggressive/externalizing behavior.
sources.relevance_notes: More speculative behavioral extension; flagged to avoid sensationalism, included for completeness.

sources.title: Lyme neuroborreliosis presenting with alexithymia and suicide attempts
sources.key_findings: Documents a neuroborreliosis case with suicidality that improved with treatment of the infection.
sources.relevance_notes: Case-level evidence that active CNS infection can produce reversible suicidality.

sources.title: Role of inflammation in suicide: from mechanisms to treatment
sources.key_findings: Reviews inflammation and the kynurenine pathway in suicidality, including quinolinic acid as an NMDA agonist/excitotoxin.
sources.relevance_notes: Mainstream mechanistic backbone any infection-suicide hypothesis relies on.

sources.title: Connecting inflammation with glutamate agonism in suicidality (CSF quinolinic acid in suicide attempters)
sources.key_findings: Found elevated CSF quinolinic acid in suicide attempters, linking inflammation to glutamatergic excitotoxicity in suicidality.
sources.relevance_notes: Direct human evidence for the quinolinic-acid/suicide link invoked by the Lyme hypothesis.

sources.title: Epidemiology of Suicide and the Psychiatric Perspective
sources.journal_or_publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
sources.key_findings: Reviews suicide epidemiology and risk factors, including chronic illness, pain, and psychosocial stressors.
sources.relevance_notes: Mainstream basis for the chronic-illness/invalidation suicide-risk pathway.

sources.title: Concurrent Lyme disease and babesiosis: evidence for increased severity and duration of illness
sources.key_findings: Co-infection increases severity and duration of illness, amplifying chronic-illness burden.
sources.relevance_notes: Links the parasitic co-infection element of this topic to elevated illness burden.

forum_excerpts.paraphrased_content: A dominant theme of hopelessness driven by not being believed: years of negative tests, dismissive clinicians, and lost work/relationships described as central to the darkest periods.
Members describe sudden uncharacteristic mood collapse or intrusive dark thoughts that feel alien to their baseline self, attributed to infection/inflammation.
Reports that the lowest mental-health points coincided with the most severe physical phases (often attributed to Babesia), improving as physical illness improved.
Many members credit peer communities with reducing isolation and providing hope and validation — a recurring protective counter-theme.
